session.hybridExplainer.activation: {lead} click the {icon} icon at the bottom-right of the message input, or default new sessions under Settings → Claude → Hybrid Mode.
session.hybridExplainer.automatic: {lead} TwiCC drives the CLI for you; the rare time it needs you on a prompt only it can show, open the Claude CLI terminal to answer.
session.hybridExplainer.change: {lead} from {date}, Anthropic bills programmatic usage — the SDK TwiCC normally runs — at full API rates, from a small monthly pool.
session.hybridExplainer.input: {lead} you still type as usual: slash commands, attachments and snippets all work like normal mode.
session.hybridExplainer.maintenance: {lead} — the copy below was written for Anthropic's programmatic-billing change announced for 15 June 2026, which has since been postponed. Hybrid mode is kept dormant behind the {flag} flag. Revisit this wording and its source link before the feature is un-gated.
session.hybridExplainer.oneWay: {lead} a hybrid session can never go back to normal mode.
session.hybridExplainer.orchestration: {lead} that's also why hybrid sessions can't be orchestrated: no human to step in. To opt Claude out entirely, turn off Enabled in orchestration under Settings → Claude.
session.hybridExplainer.plan: {lead} hybrid runs the real CLI instead, which still uses your Pro/Max quota: several times more usage for the same money.
session.hybridExplainer.preserved: {lead} the rich session view, approvals, the question widget, notifications — everything.
session.hybridExplainer.streaming: {lead} the message list shows {thinking}, then the finished reply and tools — not live; open the Claude CLI terminal to watch it stream.
session.hybridExplainer.summaryNew: Why you may {need} this in the future
session.hybridExplainer.terminal: {lead} the CLI runs in a terminal above the message input, opened on demand.
session.hybridExplainer.warning: {lead} — hybrid mode changes what your Claude usage costs.

A project can override this with its own absolute directory. Leave empty for no default.
settings.general.worktreeDirectory.label: Worktree directory template
settings.help.hint:
Help pages open by themselves the first time you reach a feature,
            and you can reopen any of them from the list below. There are only
            a few for now — the list will grow as the app evolves.
settings.layouts.saveHint: Save new layouts from a session: dock some panels, then open the layout menu (the {button} button at the right of the tab bar) and choose “Save layout”.
settings.notifications.attention.label: Agent needs your attention
settings.notifications.extraUsage.hint: Turn "Notify me" off to silence extra-usage alerts everywhere — in-app toast, sound, browser and pushed devices — without touching your per-device or per-target settings. Enabling a sound, browser notification or a pushed device turns it back on.
settings.notifications.finished.label: Agent finished working
settings.notifications.peer.hint: A peer sent you a message, or an instance asks to pair with yours. Both wait for you to act; every other peer event can wait for your next visit.
settings.notifications.peer.label: A peer needs you
settings.notifications.push.hint: Forward these notifications to external services (ntfy, Pushover, Telegram, …) using {apprise}, e.g. {example} — the {builder} can compose one for your service.
settings.notifications.push.label: Push to your devices
settings.notifications.push.missingAddre: No {address} is set, so these notifications won't link back to the session. {settings}.
settings.notifications.targets.awayHint: "Only when you're away" keeps a target silent while you're active in TwiCC on any device (desktop or phone), so it won't notify while you're at your computer — turn it off to always notify.
settings.notifications.targets.label: Targets
settings.notifications.targets.testHint: Notifications are only sent to targets whose last test succeeded (green check). A green check means the service accepted the test message — confirm it actually arrived on your device.
settings.notifications.targets.testToolt: Send a test notification to this target
settings.peers.address.changeWarning: Changing this address disables active Peer relationships and clears their credentials. You must reconnect each Peer manually.
settings.peers.address.hint: Your address, advertised to peers. Empty disables peer messaging. A different address from External serves peer traffic only; the same address keeps the whole app reachable there. HTTPS strongly recommended. The host must be reachable machine-to-machine: a tunnel-level access gate (e.g. Cloudflare Access asking for an email or Google account) blocks peer calls — use a truly public hostname.
settings.peers.address.label: Your address
settings.peers.address.useExternalAddres: Use the External address from General settings
settings.peers.name.hint: Shown to peers in your pairing requests so they know who is asking. Empty uses your address's hostname.
settings.peers.name.label: Your name

settings.presets.label: Presets
settings.providers.defaultProvider.label: Default provider for new sessions
settings.providers.enabled.hint: Disabling a provider stops all of its background tasks, prevents creating new sessions or renaming existing ones, and hides its settings section. Existing sessions remain readable.
settings.providers.enabled.label: Activated providers
settings.providers.orchestration.hint: When off, agents won't pick {provider} on their own when orchestrating sessions. You can still explicitly ask an agent to use it.
settings.providers.orchestration.label: Orchestration
settings.providers.orchestration.lastPro: At least one provider must remain enabled in orchestration.

settings.sharing.agentPermissions.artifa: Allows agents to create artifact shares whose target belongs to their own spawn subtree, and to manage artifact shares created by agents in their own spawn subtree. When enabled, agents can also revoke any existing artifact share, including links created by you, and read the URL of every existing artifact share, including links created by you or by another agent.
settings.sharing.agentPermissions.label: Agent sharing
settings.sharing.agentPermissions.sessio: Allows agents to create session shares whose target belongs to their own spawn subtree, and to manage session shares created by agents in their own spawn subtree. When enabled, agents can also revoke any existing session share, including links created by you, and read the URL of every existing session share, including links created by you or by another agent.
settings.sharing.host.hint: Dedicated share host — a hostname distinct from this app, pointing at the same port (e.g. a second tunnel hostname). Required to create share links; a different port on the same hostname is not enough. Leave empty to disable sharing.
settings.sharing.host.label: Share host
settings.shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
settings.summaries.hint: Messages and selections need at least 500 characters. Summaries target one third of the source, up to 140 words.
settings.summaries.noKey: OpenRouter is unavailable: its key is not set. Set the key in Text to Speech settings.
settings.summaries.noProvider: No Claude or Codex provider is enabled. Set an OpenRouter key or enable a provider.
settings.summaries.openrouterHint: OpenRouter uses {model}. It sends the source to OpenRouter and uses your credits.
settings.summaries.storedPreference: Stored preference: {preference}. {reason}. Effective engine: {engine}. The stored preference returns when it is available.
settings.summaries.timelineSpeechHint: On by default. Manual summaries remain available when this is off.
settings.syncHint: Sections and settings marked with a cloud icon are synced across all your devices.
settings.telemetry.payload.title: Telemetry payload
settings.terminal.config.hint: TwiCC always runs tmux on a dedicated socket per instance and forces {mouseOff} after session creation — these invariants are required for frontend selection and scroll to work. Your config is loaded first (so status bar, colors, bindings apply), then the mouse option is overridden at the session level. Leave empty to ignore any config. Applies to new terminals only.
settings.terminal.config.label: Tmux config file
settings.terminal.copyOnSelect.hint: When enabled, selecting text in a terminal with the mouse copies it to the clipboard automatically (paste with {shortcut}) — no need to click Copy. The selection stays visible.
settings.terminal.copyOnSelect.label: Copy on select
settings.terminal.copyOnSelect.primaryCl: The text goes to the regular clipboard, not the mouse "primary" selection (middle-click paste): browsers can't write to the primary selection, so middle-click won't paste it.
settings.terminal.optionKey.hint: When enabled, Option acts as the Meta key for shell shortcuts ({back}/{forward} to move word by word, {lastArgument} for the last argument), but characters typed with Option — such as {pipe}, {brace} or {backslash} on international keyboard layouts — can no longer be entered. Stored per device; applies to open terminals immediately.
settings.terminal.optionKey.label: Option key (⌥)
settings.terminal.persistence.hint: Tmux sessions are destroyed when their agent session is archived.
settings.terminal.persistence.label: Persistent sessions (tmux)
settings.textToSpeech.adaptHint: A small model rewrites the message for the ear before it is read.
settings.textToSpeech.changedWarning: This config changed since its last test: the read-aloud buttons are hidden until a new test is confirmed.
settings.textToSpeech.help: How does text to speech work?
settings.textToSpeech.intro: Read the chat messages aloud with OpenRouter, or with your own script. See the {guide} and the {models}. Prices are OpenRouter's list prices: the real cost can differ.
settings.textToSpeech.keyLoaded: {apiKey} is loaded. After you change it in {path}, restart TwiCC.
settings.textToSpeech.keyMissing: Add {apiKey} to {path}, then restart TwiCC. Testing OpenRouter configs and the OpenRouter adaptation are disabled until then.
settings.textToSpeech.modelsFailed: The OpenRouter model list did not load.

settings.textToSpeech.notePlaceholder: Optional notes about this choice, for you only
settings.textToSpeech.openRouterAdaptHin: OpenRouter uses {model}; it sends the text to OpenRouter, paid on your OpenRouter account.
settings.textToSpeech.scriptHelp: The text goes to the command's standard input; the audio (or a file path) comes back on its standard output. The help at the top of this section tells the rest.
settings.tips.manualHint: Tips will only appear when you click them from the list below.
settings.tips.resetHint: This will mark all tips as unseen. They may appear again on the next tick.
settings.titles.model.disabledProviderHi: Your choice is kept, and comes back as soon as you enable its provider again.
settings.titles.model.fallbackHint: If the selected model cannot be used — disabled, over quota, or failing — TwiCC generates the title with another model, when one is available.
settings.titles.model.matchProvider: Match session provider — {claudeModel} for Claude Code, {codexModel} for Codex
settings.titles.model.openRouterHint: — much faster: a title in under a second instead of several; uses {model}; sends the user messages to OpenRouter, paid on your OpenRouter account
settings.titles.model.openRouterSetupHin: Your choice is kept, and comes back once the OpenRouter key is set and TwiCC restarted.
settings.titles.model.providerFallbackHi: If the selected provider cannot be used — disabled, over quota, or failing — TwiCC generates the title with the other provider, when that one is enabled.

settings.usage.dumpFile.helpDescription: Save the raw API response to a JSON file each time TwiCC fetches usage data. Useful if you want to share the data with other tools without extra API calls.
settings.usage.dumpFile.label: Dump usage to file***
settings.usage.extraQuota.label: Show extra usage quota
settings.usage.extraUsageNotification.hi: Alerts you when a provider starts consuming its extra usage credits again after a quiet period. See the {notificationsLink} tab for sound, browser and pushed-device options.
settings.usage.filePath.hint: Press Apply or Enter to validate and save the path.
settings.usage.fiveHourQuota.hint: Depending on your plan, the 5-hour usage quota does not exist. If that applies to you, you can hide it. | Depending on your plans, the 5-hour usage quota does not exist. If that applies to you, you can hide it.
settings.usage.fiveHourQuota.label: 5-hour usage quota
settings.usage.history.noData: No data available for this period
settings.usage.history.title: Usage History
settings.usage.readFile.helpDescription: If you already maintain a JSON file with usage data outside TwiCC (typically because the provider's API is rate-limited), point to it here and TwiCC will read from this file instead of calling the API directly.
settings.usage.readFile.label: Read usage from file**
settings.usage.wakeUp.helpDescription: A provider's 5-hour quota window starts on its first request and resets 5 hours later, so opening it earlier fits more windows into your working day. Pick a time and TwiCC sends a tiny throwaway request at that hour each day to start the window early — skipped if one is already running. It only fires while TwiCC is running at that time (no catch-up if it was off).
settings.usage.wakeUp.label: Quota wake-up*
